drug_class: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (PD-1 blocker) combined with a subcutaneous delivery enhancer
purpose: This medication is used to treat several types of cancer, including certain skin cancers, lung cancers, and other tumors. It works by helping your immune system find and fight cancer cells. Your doctor may use it alone or with other cancer treatments depending on your specific cancer type.
how_it_works: Your immune system has natural 'brakes' that cancer cells can hijack to hide from it. Pembrolizumab releases those brakes so your immune system can recognize and attack the cancer cells. The hyaluronidase ingredient is a helper that allows the medication to be given as a shot under the skin instead of through an IV, by temporarily loosening the tissue so the medicine spreads properly.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include tiredness, itching, rash, nausea, diarrhea, joint or muscle pain, decreased appetite, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or swelling. Some people also notice changes in their lab values like low thyroid hormone levels.
warnings: This medicine can cause your immune system to become overactive and attack healthy organs, including the lungs, liver, intestines, kidneys, and hormone glands — this can be serious or even life-threatening. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, severe diarrhea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual weight gain or loss. Avoid this medication if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm the baby. Always tell your care team about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous shot), usually once every 3 or 6 weeks depending on your treatment plan. Your healthcare team will give you this shot at a clinic or infusion center — you do not give it to yourself at home. Each session typically takes only a few minutes compared to a longer IV infusion.
